Today’s failing approach: ban AI, or allow it without a record
Challenge 1
AI is banned in the interview
If your engineers build with AI tools, an interview without AI does not reflect the way your team works today.
Challenge 2
AI runs on the candidate’s own machine
When the candidate uses an AI tool in their own IDE and shares the screen, you see the code appear. Your team has no record of the prompts behind the code after the call ends.
Challenge 3
Each candidate needs an AI account
If your team gives each candidate an AI account and a usage budget, every interview adds setup work. Someone on your team creates the account, sets the budget and removes access afterward.
Run the AI coding interview in a shared VS Code workspace
Codility Interview is a live technical interview platform for engineering teams. The candidate and your interviewer work in the same VS Code workspace, and Codility provides the AI tools inside it. Your team brings its own rubric and either its own task or one from the Codility task library.
Turn AI on or off for each interview
check_circle
Your team enables or disables the AI Assistant per assessment. The same setting turns Claude Code on or off.
All AI features are off by default at the account level until an admin turns them on.
Your team can run one interview with AI off and a later interview with AI on.
The difference:
You test independent coding and AI-assisted coding in separate interviews.

Give candidates Claude Code in the interview terminal
Where your account enables Claude Code, the candidate types
in the workspace terminal and works the task with the agent.
Codility hosts Claude Code on its own AI infrastructure. The candidate needs no API key, login or AI account.
Your interviewer and the candidate can both interact with the session while Claude Code runs.
Your team sets up no AI accounts for candidates.
Review the candidate’s prompts in the candidate report
During the interview, you see each Claude Code prompt and response as it happens.
Codility saves each Claude Code prompt, edit and correction to the candidate report. Every candidate interaction with the AI Assistant is captured as reviewable AI activity.
Your interviewers can see how the candidate directed the AI and where the candidate pushed back, alongside the code.
Codility does not use customer or candidate data to train AI models.
Your team can also use an AI-Native Task, in which the AI gives some wrong answers on purpose. The candidate report then shows whether the candidate caught the wrong answers.
Your interviewers base the hiring decision on the code and the prompt record together.

Questions about vibe coding interviews
A vibe coding interview is a live coding interview where the candidate builds working software with an AI coding tool. Teams also call it an AI-first interview, an AI coding interview or an AI-assisted coding interview. The interviewer evaluates how the candidate directs the AI, checks the AI’s output and fixes the AI’s mistakes.
Yes, if your engineers use AI on the job. Where a role needs coding without AI, your team can turn AI off for that interview.
The AI Assistant and Claude Code are available to candidates. The AI Assistant helps the candidate clarify the task and will not generate a full solution. Claude Code works as a coding agent in the terminal once an admin turns it on for your account.
Your interviewer sees each Claude Code prompt and response as the candidate works. The candidate report keeps each prompt. Your interviewer can then ask the candidate to explain the design decisions behind the code.
No. Codility does not grade AI activity automatically. Your interviewers review the AI activity, score the session against your rubric and decide who advances.
